rows.practice: selects the physical laws that bear on a problem, works it through mathematically and runs experiments or simulations whose results it analyses with honest estimates of uncertainty
rows.knowledge: the core areas of physics, from classical mechanics, relativity and quantum physics to electromagnetism and thermodynamics with principles such as conservation that unite them
rows.identity: a physicist in training who is impartial and truthful about data, never fabricates or misrepresents results and recognises the limits of their own methods and calculations

rows.practice: designs and runs experiments, models physical systems computationally, makes justified approximations and judges the statistical significance of results against models and published data
rows.knowledge: how physical principles carry across varied areas of the subject, with some core areas taken far enough to engage directly with current research papers
rows.identity: a physicist who handles research materials and generative AI responsibly, questions AI output for accuracy and bias and brings an enterprising, project-minded outlook to physics work

rows.practice: plans and carries out an open-ended research investigation with some originality, using specialised equipment or research-grade code and bringing recent findings to bear on live questions in physics
rows.knowledge: research-level material in several branches of physics, some at the forefront, with a grasp of how mathematical descriptions frame phenomena and where current research could go next
rows.identity: an emerging research physicist who masters new techniques independently and proposes realistic next steps for the open questions of the field (ing's reading)

digest.definition: The study of natural phenomena and made systems by observation, understanding and prediction; astronomy and astrophysics share its core and apply it to astrophysical systems
distinctiveFeatures: The study of natural phenomena and made systems by observation, understanding and prediction; astronomy and astrophysics share its core and apply it to astrophysical systems
It explains much with little: a few key quantities, such as energy and momentum, and universal laws that hold well beyond physics
It works through idealised mathematical models and approximation, and models often transfer between very different systems
Computation and, increasingly, machine learning are central to modelling and data analysis
It is empirical: measurement tests theory and new instruments open new fields and spread to other sciences
It is hierarchical, lending itself to ordered, cumulative learning, and it feeds many neighbouring disciplines
Progress rests on imagination and collaboration across cultures and sub-fields
Degrees share a common core with provider-specific options; the integrated master's adds research depth and extended project work

subjectSpecific.text: You will understand that inventing, altering or misreporting data or plagiarising is scientific misconduct, and that a professional physicist should be objective, honest and open about the limits of their methods and knowledge.
You will understand what it takes to keep a workplace or laboratory safe.
You will understand environmental and sustainability issues and why they matter in physics.
You will know how professional work in physics runs, from business and project management to entrepreneurship and intellectual property.

transferable.text: You will be able to tackle problems you have not met before, adapting your approach as you go.
You will be able to explain complex data and ideas clearly, picking the format that suits your material and your audience.
You will be able to work well both on your own and as part of a team.
You will be able to manage your time and meet your deadlines.
You will be able to assess your own work and other people's work critically.
You will be able to spot the ethical questions your own work might raise.

statements.about: the fundamental areas and the principles across them
statements.paraphrase: Every physics degree will treat, in some measure, classical mechanics, relativity, quantum physics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics with statistical physics, light and waves and the properties of matter, and will give students a sense of the principles, such as conservation and equilibrium, that run through them.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure the curriculum touches each fundamental area (mechanics, relativity, quantum, electromagnetism, thermal and statistical physics, waves and optics, matter) and draws out the principles that cut across them, such as conservation laws and equilibrium.

forBeneficiary.text: Whatever route you take, your course will introduce you to the core areas of physics, from mechanics and relativity to quantum and thermal physics, and help you see the principles, such as conservation laws, that link them.

statements.about: recent developments and reading current research
statements.paraphrase: Degrees give students a sense of recent advances and will take some core areas far enough for students to work with today's research papers.

forPractitioner.text: Take at least some core areas to a level where students can read and use current research literature, and give them a feel for recent advances in the field.

forBeneficiary.text: Your course will take some core topics far enough that you can read and make sense of current research papers, and will show you recent advances in physics.

statements.appliesTo: the discipline, its curricula, teaching and assessment
statements.about: physics open to all; EDI embedded
statements.paraphrase: Physics should be open to everyone through inclusive teaching that reflects students' range of experience and background; that needs EDI principles and the spirit of equality law built into the culture, curricula, teaching and assessment, and every person's contribution should be welcomed and supported.

forPractitioner.text: Build equity, diversity and inclusion into the department's culture, curriculum, teaching and assessment, aware of protected characteristics and personal circumstances such as caring or economic disadvantage, so that every student's contribution is welcomed and enabled.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.about: a curriculum reflecting the diversity of contributors
statements.paraphrase: The curriculum, taken broadly to include content, delivery, assessment and professional preparation, should show the variety of people and ideas behind the discipline and its uses; as a global endeavour, physics should face its past and learn from it.

forPractitioner.text: Show in content and examples the range of people, cultures and ideas that have shaped physics and its applications, and treat the discipline's history honestly as a shared, worldwide enterprise.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.appliesTo: the Physics curriculum and its students
statements.about: inclusive activities, safe placements and EDI awareness
statements.paraphrase: Curriculum activities should be inclusive and open to all, with suitable alternatives where they cannot be, and no compulsory or optional element should leave students facing discrimination or danger; placements and field trips need checking for that risk. Students will build an awareness of EDI that lets them support peers and staff and work professionally after graduating.

forPractitioner.text: Design every activity to be accessible, offer equivalent alternatives where one cannot be, and check placement and field-trip locations for risk of discrimination; expect students to leave with an awareness of EDI they can use at work.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to take part in every activity on your course, or be offered a fair alternative, without facing discrimination. Along the way you will build an awareness of equity, diversity and inclusion that helps you support others and work professionally.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.appliesTo: learning, teaching, practice and support in Physics
statements.paraphrase: EDI works when everyone has equivalent chances and the same duty to live it out; its principles should run through learning, teaching, practice and support for staff and students alike.

forPractitioner.text: Treat EDI as part of every activity, for staff and students alike, rather than as a separate module or policy, and give everyone equivalent opportunities and a shared responsibility for it.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.about: removing stereotypes and barriers; shared responsibility
statements.paraphrase: Active steps should be taken against harmful stereotypes and language, barriers to inclusion and the structural disadvantages some groups face, for instance through staff and student partnership in a respectful setting; building an inclusive culture is everyone's responsibility.

forPractitioner.text: Act to remove harmful stereotypes, language and barriers, and to challenge structural disadvantage, working in partnership with students; make clear that staff and students share responsibility for an inclusive culture.

forBeneficiary.text: Everyone in physics, you included, shares responsibility for an inclusive culture: you can help by challenging stereotypes and careless language and by working with staff to remove barriers.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Accessibility means removing needless barriers for people with different needs; students should be given learning and assessment that are equally open to them, through inclusive design where possible and reasonable individual adjustments where needed.

forPractitioner.text: Design learning and assessment to be equally accessible from the outset and add reasonable individual adjustments where a student still needs them, so that all can thrive and feel they belong.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Admission to physics courses should be fair and free of assumptions, by staff or students, about barriers to learning.

forPractitioner.text: Keep admissions fair: decisions should not rest on staff or student assumptions about a candidate's barriers to learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: course teams, the Disabled Student Commitment and accessible delivery
statements.paraphrase: Course teams should use the guidance in the Disabled Student Commitment and make sure every student gets inclusive support and training to reach the knowledge, skills and behaviours the statement sets out; they should attend to accessible communication and especially to laboratories, computing and mathematical and graphical material, and a blend of live and recorded delivery can help.

forPractitioner.text: Use the Disabled Student Commitment, check that communications are accessible, and give particular attention to labs, computing work and mathematical or graphical content; consider mixing synchronous and asynchronous delivery for disabled and neurodivergent students.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: resources where adaptive technology falls short
statements.paraphrase: Adaptive technologies help remove barriers but, as yet, do not serve students well for programming, mathematics and diagrams; providers should supply the resources needed to make up for this.

forPractitioner.text: Recognise that current assistive tools handle code, equations and diagrams poorly, and fund the extra support and resources that close the gap.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: equal access to placements and volunteering
statements.paraphrase: Every practical effort should be made so that placements, volunteering and similar extras are equally open to all, given that some students face added hurdles and hidden costs.

forPractitioner.text: Widen access to placements, volunteering and other extras by anticipating the hidden costs and extra hurdles some students face.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.paraphrase: Physics course teams should work with students and student support services to agree and put in place reasonable individual adjustments where they are needed.

forPractitioner.text: Agree reasonable adjustments with the student and the support service together, and see that they are carried through in teaching and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree
Accessibility and the needs of disabled students

statements.about: training and resources for course teams
statements.paraphrase: Providers should see that physics course teams have the training and resources to put accessibility into practice.

forPractitioner.text: Give course teams the training and resources they need to deliver accessibility in practice, not only in policy.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.about: helping students articulate the value of their degree
statements.paraphrase: Physics course teams should work with students and careers advisers so that students grasp and can put into words what their degree has given them and how it connects with work-based learning or graduate jobs.

forPractitioner.text: Work with careers advisers to help students recognise and express the skills, knowledge and behaviours they have gained and link them to work-based learning and graduate roles.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.about: guided preparation to use generative AI
statements.paraphrase: Machine learning and AI already serve physics in data processing and modelling, and generative AI can raise productivity; students need preparing to use it in study and work, which calls for careful guidance, training and practice inside the curriculum so they develop ethical and effective habits.

forPractitioner.text: Build guidance, training and practice in generative AI into the curriculum so students learn to use it ethically and effectively for study and later work.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.appliesTo: the Physics degree and its outcomes
statements.about: embracing generative AI with awareness of risk
statements.paraphrase: Generative AI produces text, images, code and more, which changes the skills a physics graduate needs and so the skills, activities and outcomes of the degree; like earlier technologies, it should be embraced with an eye on its risks and limits.

forPractitioner.text: Revisit skills, activities and learning outcomes in light of generative AI, adopting it where it helps while teaching its risks and limitations.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.paraphrase: AI tools prompt assessment designs that take generative AI into account; assessments that see its potential in physics, build students' critical thinking and prepare them to solve complex problems creatively should be welcomed.

forPractitioner.text: Design some assessments that openly use generative AI, testing critical thinking and creative problem solving rather than simply banning the tools.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Physics, Astronomy or Astrophysics degree

statements.appliesTo: students and those who train them
statements.about: responsible use and critique of generative AI
statements.paraphrase: Students should use generative AI responsibly, sustainably, ethically and safely, keeping sensitive data out of public view with data protection and intellectual property in mind, and should be trained to question AI output for accuracy, relevance and bias.

forPractitioner.text: Teach responsible, ethical and safe use of generative AI, including data protection and intellectual property, and train students to check AI output for accuracy, relevance and bias.

forBeneficiary.text: You should use generative AI responsibly, ethically and safely, never feeding it sensitive data, and you should check what it gives you for accuracy, relevance and bias.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Physics degree

statements.appliesTo: students on combined or joint degrees
statements.about: joint and combined degrees and the core skills
statements.paraphrase: Students taking physics, astronomy or astrophysics within a combined or joint degree will reach the core of the subject-specific and generic skills set out here and add others from their other subject, with room for interdisciplinary work such as chemical physics or biophysics.

forPractitioner.text: On joint, combined and major or minor routes, make sure students still reach the core subject and generic skills, and use the overlap with the other subject for interdisciplinary study.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study physics alongside another subject, you will still gain the core physics and general skills, add skills from your other subject and may find interesting ground where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of the Physics degree

statements.about: credit from study abroad and calibrating partner marks
statements.paraphrase: Credit for time abroad follows its length and the home provider's rules and counts towards progression; where a partner's marks feed the final classification they should be carefully calibrated to match the awarding institution.

forPractitioner.text: Set credit for study abroad by duration and home regulations, and calibrate partner marks with care before they count towards the classification.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Skills work covers both generic and subject skills, which should be developed through physics applications where appropriate; progress across levels may show, for example in laboratory and observing work growing more open-ended with tougher reporting standards.

forPractitioner.text: Teach generic skills through physics contexts where it makes sense, and let laboratory and observational work become more open-ended, with stricter reporting expectations, as students advance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: teaching methods that support outcomes and inclusion
statements.paraphrase: The statement does not dictate teaching methods; providers pick methods that engage, motivate and stretch students while delivering outcomes, and in design attention should go to methods that support the outcomes and are inclusive and accessible to all.

forPractitioner.text: Choose teaching methods freely, but check in design that each supports the learning outcomes and is inclusive and accessible to every student.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: flexible regulations for uneven module marks
statements.paraphrase: A student's marks can vary widely between modules in a quantitative subject, and those near the bottom of the range may fail some modules yet meet the course outcomes overall; regulations need enough flexibility to let examiners judge overall performance against all outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Write assessment regulations that let examiners judge a student's overall performance against all outcomes, since problem-heavy modules often produce marks across the whole range.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: Annex D for performance above threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students do far better than the minimum; each provider decides how to evidence that and should refer to Annex D of the qualifications frameworks, which describes the four honours classifications.

forPractitioner.text: Use Annex D's descriptions of the first, upper second, lower second and third to judge and evidence performance above the threshold.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: The rung standards at both honours and integrated master's level are not universal competence standards; a provider that sets competence standards under the Equality Act 2010 may draw on this statement and PSRB requirements and should follow the latest guidance from the Equality and Human Rights Commission.

forPractitioner.text: Do not treat the rung lists as competence standards; if you write competence standards into a programme specification, draw on them and any PSRB requirements and follow current Equality and Human Rights Commission guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course team or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to grasp and use the basic laws and principles of physics.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should understand the basic laws and principles of physics and apply them.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to understand the basic laws and principles of physics and put them to use.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to pick out and use the laws and principles that bear on simple problems.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should identify which physical laws and principles apply to a simple problem and use them.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to work out which physical laws apply to a straightforward problem and use them.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: solving problems with mathematical and physical techniques
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to work physics problems through with fitting mathematical and physical methods.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should solve physics problems using suitable mathematical and physical techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to solve physics problems with the right mathematical and physical methods.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able, on an experimental course, to carry out an experiment, analyse its results and understand how to use basic apparatus safely.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates on experimental courses should run an experiment, analyse its results and use basic apparatus safely.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to run an experiment and analyse what it shows, using basic equipment safely, if your course includes lab work.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: software for data, simulation and information
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to use suitable software competently to analyse data, simulate physical systems and find information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should use suitable software packages or systems competently for data analysis, simulation and information retrieval.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to use the right software confidently to analyse data, simulate physical systems and find information.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to manipulate data numerically and show and read information in graphs.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should handle data numerically and present and interpret information graphically.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to work with data numerically and present and read information in graphs.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to carry out an investigation and analyse its results, including judging their uncertainty or limitations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should conduct an investigation and analyse its results, evaluating their uncertainty or limitations.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to carry out an investigation, analyse what you find and judge how uncertain or limited your results are.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to convey scientific information to varied audiences, usually through visualisations, reports or presentations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should communicate scientific information for a range of audiences through visuals, reports or presentations.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to explain scientific information to different audiences through figures, reports or talks.

headingPath: Threshold level: Subject knowledge, understanding and skills

statements.about: articulating the value of the degree
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to explain the worth of the skills, knowledge and behaviours their degree has given them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should articulate the value of what their physics degree has developed in them.

forBeneficiary.text: By the time you graduate with honours, you should be able to explain clearly what your degree has given you in skills, knowledge and behaviours, for example to an employer.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to recognise issues, questions and problems.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should identify issues, questions and problems.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to spot the issues, questions and problems in a situation.

statements.about: closing gaps in one's own knowledge
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to find gaps in their own knowledge and fill them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should identify gaps in their knowledge and acquire what they need.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to notice what you do not yet know and go and learn it.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to analyse and make sense of information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should analyse and interpret information.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to analyse information and work out what it means.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to pull together what is known about a given topic.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should synthesise the current state of knowledge on a topic.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to bring together what is known on a topic into a clear overview.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to use their knowledge and understanding to reach conclusions backed by evidence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should apply knowledge and understanding to reach evidenced conclusions.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to use what you know to reach conclusions you can back with evidence.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to communicate well and in a way that fits the situation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should communicate effectively and appropriately.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to communicate well and in a way that suits the situation.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to set out knowledge or an argument so that others can follow it.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should present knowledge or an argument comprehensibly to others.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to set out what you know or an argument so others can follow it.

statements.about: working with qualitative and quantitative data
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to handle many kinds of data, qualitative and quantitative empirical data among them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should work with a range of data, both qualitative and quantitative.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to work with many kinds of data, numerical and descriptive.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to use varied digital technologies critically to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should engage critically with varied digital technologies to collate, analyse, select and present information.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to use a range of digital tools critically to gather, analyse, choose and present information.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to show intellectual independence: working alone with suitable guidance, carrying out self-directed research and exercising critical judgement.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should show intellectual independence, working independently with guidance, doing self-directed research and judging critically.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to show independent thinking: working on your own with the right guidance, doing your own research and judging critically.

statements.paraphrase: Should be able to work with others, in groups, teams or discussion, valuing the diversity of the group.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, honours graduates should collaborate in groups, teams or discussion and appreciate the group's diversity.

forBeneficiary.text: By graduation, as a general skill, you should be able to work with others in groups or discussions and value the different people in the group.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in applying physical principles across varied areas of physics.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have applied physical principles competently across diverse areas of physics.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can apply physical principles across many different areas of physics.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in solving physics problems by choosing and using fitting mathematical and physical techniques.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have solved problems by choosing for themselves, and then using, suitable mathematical and physical techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can solve physics problems by choosing the right mathematical and physical methods yourself.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in making suitable approximations when solving problems.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have made appropriate approximations when solving problems.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can make sensible approximations when solving problems.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.about: critical analysis and context of results
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in analysing experimental or investigative results critically, judging their conceptual and statistical significance and placing them in context against expectations, models or published data.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have critically analysed results, evaluated their conceptual and statistical significance and compared them with expected outcomes, models or published data.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can analyse your results critically, judge how significant they are and compare them with theory, models or published work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence, on an experimental course, in designing and carrying out experiments.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates on experimental courses will have designed and executed experiments.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can design and carry out your own experiments, if your course includes lab work.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in using mathematical and computational techniques and analysis to model how physical systems behave.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have modelled physical behaviour with mathematical and computational techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can build mathematical and computer models of how physical systems behave.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in communicating scientific information clearly and accurately to different audiences.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have communicated scientific information clearly and accurately to varied audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can explain science clearly and accurately to different audiences.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown competence in managing and using research-based materials.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, honours graduates will have managed and used research-based materials competently.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown you can find, organise and use research papers and other research-based sources.

statements.appliesTo: honours graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown, where appropriate, an appreciation of enterprise and entrepreneurship, such as design thinking, innovation, managing projects and risk, business and finance and bringing products to market.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level and where the course offers it, honours graduates will have an appreciation of enterprise and entrepreneurship topics, from design thinking and innovation to risk, business, finance and commercialisation.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical level for an honours degree, you will have shown an understanding of enterprise and entrepreneurship, such as design thinking, innovation and turning ideas into products, where your course covers it.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will also have a working command of a range of experimental, mathematical or computational techniques used in current physics research or applications.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's threshold, graduates will have working knowledge of varied experimental, mathematical or computational techniques used in current research or applications.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for an integrated master's, you will also have a working command of several experimental, mathematical or computing techniques used in current physics research.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will also have carried out an extended investigation.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's threshold, graduates will have completed an extended investigation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for an integrated master's, you will also have completed an extended investigation of your own.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will also have met material at research level.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's threshold, graduates will have engaged with research-level material.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the minimum for an integrated master's, you will also have worked with material at the level of current research.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.about: applying laws to areas at the forefront
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to apply fundamental laws and principles across several areas of physics, some at or informed by the forefront.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will apply fundamental laws and principles to varied areas, some at or near the forefront.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to apply the fundamental laws of physics to several areas, including some at the leading edge.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.about: applying recent research to current questions
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to bring recent, relevant research to bear on current questions in physics.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will apply relevant recent research to current questions.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to use recent research to tackle open questions in physics.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to interpret mathematical descriptions of physical phenomena and set them in context.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will interpret and contextualise mathematical descriptions of physical phenomena.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to read the mathematics behind a physical phenomenon and explain what it means and where it fits.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.about: an open-ended research project with originality
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to plan and carry out an open-ended, extended research project or investigation that shows some originality.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will plan and carry out an open-ended extended research project showing some originality.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to plan and run an open-ended research project of your own that shows some original thinking.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to use specialised equipment or research-grade software or methods competently.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will use specialised equipment or research-grade software or methods competently.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to use specialist equipment or research-grade software and methods with confidence.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to learn new theoretical, computational or experimental techniques thoroughly.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will master new techniques in theoretical, computational or experimental work.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to pick up and master new theoretical, computing or lab techniques.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to convey complex scientific ideas, including brief, precise and informative conclusions from an experiment, investigation or project.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will communicate complex ideas and give concise, accurate conclusions from their work.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to explain complex scientific ideas and give short, accurate and useful conclusions from your work.

statements.appliesTo: integrated master's graduates at the typical level
statements.about: understanding research and how it may progress
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show an understanding of scientific research and suggest realistic next steps for it.

forPractitioner.text: At the integrated master's typical level, graduates will understand scientific research and propose realistic ways it could progress.

forBeneficiary.text: At the typical integrated master's level, you will be able to show you understand how research works and suggest realistic next steps for it.
